name: ABANDONED CLAIM ROW
materialIdentity: Eleven abandoned claims in a row on a worked hillside, their markers before their holes, a path worn deep in front; night, the town's hour (errata 98, 99)
note: Room 27, doc 20: the abandoned claim row, in the diggings below the road to the claims (errata 99 A, C). 'Nobody comes up here' (doc 08).

LOOK_AT.say: One boot. Good quality, once. It is not paired with anything.
repeat: A left boot. I looked at the other markers for a right one. There isn't one.
Good stitching, gone gray. Somebody paid a month's wages for this boot and walked out of it.
Wind across the top of it, a hollow little hoot.
Nothing. It is waiting for the other one, and so, a little, am I.

LOOK_AT.say: The first marker in the row. EUREKA, it says, dated the spring of the rush.
repeat: Dated the spring of the rush. He was among the first, and the first to be wrong.
Someone has scratched a small question mark after it. Not the same hand. A later, sadder hand.
then: He found the name and nothing else.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind on split wood. The exclamation has weathered off.
repeat: The board ticks in the sun. It has dried out, like the word.
Nothing. Eureka is a word you only get to say once.

LOOK_AT.say: PROVIDENCE. A Rhode Island man, then.
repeat: The lettering is careful, the hand schooled. Somebody's mother taught him that hand, in the same town as mine.
I find I've stood here longer than at the others. I'm not going to examine why.
then: We are three thousand miles from the reference and it did not help him either.

repeat: Wind across the face of it. It sounds like a Sunday afternoon a long way off.
Nothing. The reference is lost on the territory.

LOOK_AT.say: THE SURE THING. The paint outlasted the certainty.
repeat: Beneath the name, smaller, a date, and smaller still, a second date. On the second, he was sure of something else.
It is the best-made marker in the row. He was sure of the carpentry, at least.

LISTEN_TO.say: A loose nail, ringing faintly. The one sure thing on the claim.
repeat: The nail again, ringing when the wind leans.
The nail, and then nothing. Even the one sure thing is working loose.

LOOK_AT.say: PATIENCE. Abandoned second in the row, the register says.
repeat: The paint is thick and careful, laid on in three coats. He had time for that, at the beginning.
Nobody has filed on it since. The town learned something here and will not say what.
then: There is a lesson and nobody wants it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing at all. It ran out.
repeat: Nothing. Not even the wind waits here long.
Nothing. It was very patient, and then it was not.

LOOK_AT.say: THE MOTHERLODE, in letters that used up two boards. Ambition at marker scale.
repeat: He painted the O's as nuggets. He had the whole thing planned, except the gold.
Knee deep. I measured it against my own knee. The hole never came up to the name.
then: The hole behind it is knee deep.

LISTEN_TO.say: Both boards knock in the wind, out of time with each other.
repeat: The two boards knocking, one for MOTHER and one for LODE, and they have never agreed.
A slow double knock, like someone at a door who does not expect an answer.

overrides.PUSH: Both boards knocked, out of time. Even leaning on it, you can hear the argument the name lost.

LOOK_AT.say: LUCKY DAN'S. Dan, the story goes, left the territory with money — from selling this marker's claim to the next optimist. The luck was real. It was just all in the leaving.
repeat: DAN'S is in bigger letters than LUCKY. He knew which part he could count on.
Three men bought this claim from each other after Dan. None of them changed the marker. It was the only thing on it with any value.

LISTEN_TO.say: A creak with a rhythm to it. Almost a chuckle.
repeat: The creak again, with its rhythm. Dan, laughing all the way to Sacramento.
Nothing. The joke has been told, and Dan has gone with the punchline.

overrides.PICK_UP: I considered taking the marker as a lesson. But the lesson is load-bearing where it stands.

LOOK_AT.say: BONANZA, misspelled BONANSA, corrected, the correction misspelled.
repeat: The last attempt is the smallest, squeezed in at the edge. He ran out of board and patience together.
Somebody has since corrected it a fourth time, in chalk, and got it right. Too late to matter to anyone.
then: He fought that word to a draw and the ground beat him.

repeat: Nothing. Neither side is talking.
Wind in the letters. Even it cannot decide on the Z.

LOOK_AT.say: GLORY HOLE. A mining term, I'm assured. The hole is there. The glory is on back order.
repeat: The shaft goes deeper than any other on the row. He was the most certain or the most stubborn, and out here they look the same.
His initials are cut into the lip of the shaft, at the height of a man sitting on the edge. By the wear, he sat there a long time.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind across the shaft mouth below. A low note, held.
repeat: The low note again, held as long as the wind holds it.
The note, falling away. The shaft lets it go, the way it let everything go.

LOOK_AT.say: THE WIDOW'S MITE. Small letters, careful hand.
repeat: The workings are no wider than her shoulders. She dug them to fit herself, exactly.
Somebody keeps the marker upright. Not straightened — kept. A stone has been set at its foot, and replaced.
then: Whoever she was, she dug it herself; the workings are narrow and exact.

LISTEN_TO.say: The quietest marker in the row. Even the wind lowers its voice.
repeat: Very quiet. The wind goes round it.
Nothing, and a different nothing from the others. It sounds attended to.

LOOK_AT.say: NEW CANAAN. The promised land, claimed and quit inside one summer.
repeat: On the back, under AND THE LORD, the ghost of more words, gone too pale to follow.
Claimed and quit in one summer. The promised land took less time to leave than to reach.
then: The scripture on the reverse has weathered down to 'AND THE LORD.'

LISTEN_TO.say: Split wood, breathing with the heat. The sermon continues at a whisper.
repeat: Split wood, ticking. The sermon has reached a pause.
Nothing. The congregation has gone home.

LOOK_AT.say: The last marker has no name at all. Either he never chose one or he took it with him.
repeat: Not weathered off. Never painted. The wood is as clean as the day it was set.
The workings behind it are the deepest on the row. Whoever he was, he did not need a name to dig.
then: Of the eleven, this is the one I think about.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Not a thing. It never said, and it isn't starting now.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing.

overrides.TALK_TO: I asked its name. The wind declined on its behalf. Of the eleven, it is still the one I think about.

LOOK_AT.say: The frames of old sluices, their boards long since borrowed for something else.
repeat: One still has its riffles, nailed in hope and left in place.
The water they were built for went somewhere else a season later. Even the creek left the row.
then: The skeleton of an idea about water.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind through the frames, a dry rattle where water should be.
repeat: A loose board tapping, as if asking to be used.
Nothing. They have been dry long enough to forget.

LOOK_AT.say: Eleven holes. Some of them are forty feet deep. Somebody dug forty feet by hand and then stopped and walked away, and I'd like to know which day he decided.
repeat: Every hole on the row is a different depth, and every depth is a different day somebody gave up.
Some were filled back in, neatly. Most were not. You can tell the tidy men from here.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind, in the holes. It's a low sound.
repeat: Wind in the holes, eleven notes, none of them in tune with another.
Nothing, in a lull. Eleven holes, holding their breath.
then: It is almost the same sound as my hole and it is not the same sound at all.

LOOK_AT.say: A path, worn deep, between eleven claims that produced nothing.
repeat: Worn down past the topsoil to the hardpan. A great many days went into this path.
It is the one thing on the row that was finished.
then: Somebody walked this every day for a long time.

repeat: My own boots on it, and nobody else's.
Nothing. The path has outlasted every reason to walk it.
